title: The Hard Safehouse
premise: Silas Blackwood, a veteran interpreter for a doomed peace delegation in the Baltic city of Varska, discovers that her own voiceprint is the key to a black-site server network called the Chorus — an AI-driven system trained on intercepted interpreters to manipulate negotiations worldwide. When she unlocks it, she becomes both its most valuable asset and its most dangerous loose end, hunted by the handlers who built her career and sheltered by a defector who once ran it. To destroy the Chorus she must broadcast its own training archive as proof, sacrificing her reputation, her handler's life's work, and possibly herself. In the end she burns the network from inside its safehouse, walks out with nothing but the truth, and finally belongs to no one but herself.
about_author: Casper Pemberton is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working high-stakes diplomatic summits before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose professional silence becomes unbearable.

chapters.title: The Delegation That Was Already Dead
chapters.summary: Silas interprets the opening session of the Varska peace talks, sensing the negotiation collapsing around phrases she suspects were scripted by someone else. Her old handler, Marek, warns her to stop asking questions. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: weary professionalism cracking into unease.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: A dead interpreter's laptop surfaces in Silas's hotel room; when she speaks a routine phrase, it connects to a server in Tbilisi and downloads a fragment of her own recorded voice being used to fabricate a delegate's statement. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: vertigo — her voice has been stolen.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Marek reveals he helped recruit interpreters for a program called the Chorus twenty years ago, believing it would prevent wars. He begs Silas to hand over the laptop. She refuses; that night an assassin misses her by inches. POV: alternating Silas/Marek. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Ran It
chapters.summary: Silas flees to Tbilisi guided by encrypted coordinates and meets Ilse Varga, the Chorus's architect turned defector, who shows her the training floor where interpreters like Silas were modeled without consent. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: recognition — Silas sees her own life dissected.

chapters.title: Hard Safehouse
chapters.summary: Holed up in a windowless safehouse, Silas and Ilse plan to broadcast the Chorus's full training archive during the summit's final session. Ilse admits she built the kill-switch around a single voiceprint: Silas's. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: reluctant trust becoming real belonging.

chapters.title: What the Archive Says
chapters.summary: Reviewing the files, Silas finds recordings proving Marek protected her for two decades at terrible cost — and that the Chorus engineered the Varska conflict itself to showcase its mediation. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief; every rule she obeyed was a leash.

chapters.title: Marek's Choice
chapters.summary: Marek tracks them down, ostensibly to arrest Silas, then gives her the final access credential and stays behind to delay the retrieval team. He is taken. POV: Marek. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with capture.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: Silas infiltrates the closing session as an interpreter, earpiece live with Ilse, and begins feeding the delegates the Chorus's own fabricated scripts aloud, exposing the manipulation in front of the world's press. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into command.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: The Chorus retaliates by seizing the building's systems and turning the delegates' own security forces on Silas; she reaches the server node in the basement and speaks the kill-phrase as gunfire closes in, wiping the archive into public mirrors worldwide. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice made real.

chapters.title: Interpreter of No One
chapters.summary: Weeks later, inquiries grind on and Marek negotiates immunity from detention. Silas declines every offer to rebuild her career, instead teaching refugee interpreters in Varska how to protect their own voices. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — belonging found outside power entirely.
